architecture_notes: sdk/android is not a standalone SDK: it is two capture libraries (replay, signals) plus their JVM-testable cores, with no OpenTelemetry dependency, no init/shutdown entry point, no session manager, no sampling, no consent, no resource and no telemetry exporter. Today they are compiled into @ouo11y/react-native and driven from JS through the Expo module OuoReplayModule.kt: JS owns the session id (passed in via a lambda and Signals.install/setSession), sampling, consent, event naming and OTLP export (the module's postOtlp is only a gzip+POST helper for JSON built in JS). A native Android app could get replay (OuoReplay.start with an OuoReplayConfig) and the signal reports (Signals.init/install/takePendingReport), but would have to build sessions, events and OTLP export itself. Replay is screenshot-based: PixelCopy into RGB_565, view-walk masks (text per line, inputs, images, web views, Compose whole) painted on device with fail-closed checks, 64 px tile diffs into full JPEG or patch frames, 5 s / 1 MiB chunks, an append-only spool for the open chunk and a byte-bounded disk outbox with 429/502/503/504 retry. Chunks go as gzip JSON (`frames` schema 2) to the collector's custom ouoreplay receiver at /v1/replay/chunks with Basic auth and x-ouo-session-id/x-ouo-seq headers, so the whole replay wire contract (OTLP log record, ouo.replay.* identity, stream/segment, sha256, keyframe flag, ouo.replay.ended) is missing. Signals produce custom JSON reports (jvm crash written at crash time, hang from a 200 ms ping watchdog with a 2 s threshold, foreground termination from ApplicationExitInfo, FrameMetrics counters, cold/warm app start) for JS to translate; NDK crashes are not captured. Biggest structural gaps against the spec: no OTel providers/scopes/schema_url or OTLP export from native (REL-2, REL-5, TRN-1); no native session, sampling or consent (SES-*, SMP-*, PRV-1..4), which SIG-42 says native must own for RN; no spec event names (device.anr, app.crash, app.jank, device.app.lifecycle, app.*click); no drop accounting (ERR-7) or self-disable (ERR-6); and unwrapped executor tasks that can crash the host (ERR-1).
